title: Machine-checked proof of the unique-zero conjecture (OEIS A084030)
description: theorem A084030: for every n >= 3 the witness set of row n of triangle A084029 has at least n elements — the row is full, so the diagonal term a(n) is nonzero; theorems A084030_zero_unique (a(2)=0 is the unique zero) and A084030_one (a(1)=1). Together they prove the conjecture recorded as an unsigned comment on OEIS A084029 and A084030 (entries by Amarnath Murthy, May 24 2003; extended by David Wasserman, Dec 09 2004): 'Only one term is zero.' Companion corollary theorem A084033: for n >= 3 the quotient row T(n,k)=A084029(n,k)/n has >= n integer terms, all nonzero. To our knowledge as of 2026-11-04, first written proof and first machine-checked formalization (corpus and date evidenced in VERIFICATIONS/anteriorite.md). Certification: Lean 4 + mathlib v4.35.0, pinned manifest. A084030_zero_unique and A084030_one are kernel-pure (decide); A084030 and A084033 depend on the three standard axioms plus one disclosed native_decide certificate (the 128-row witness table table029_ok_all — reduction kernel-verified, finite case check via native evaluation).
